title: Short-session priority smoothing and TTFT recovery for multi-variant fanout
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers reported a ~2.5x increase in TTFT and a 30-60% drop in tokens/sec for short conversational sessions (avg length < 80 tokens) after the model-catalog rollforward on 2026-03-05. This ticket coordinates triage, mitigation and a targeted hotfix that preserves SLA for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while we fully remediate the underlying scheduling regression.

Observed behavior: After the model catalog update, multiplexed requests to quantized model variants and float32 variants began grouping into mid-size microbatches. Continuous-batching heuristics and the kernel-selector affinity started favoring larger kernel paths (higher throughput but higher per-first-token latency) for short sequences, causing TTFT spikes and overall token-rate erosion. The problem disproportionately affected:
- short-session traffic (chat-like flows, quick Q&A)
- multi-variant fanout (requests pinned to several compatible model variants simultaneously)
- customers on Dedicated pools with mixed model families and on Private deployments with heterogeneous hardware.

Root cause hypothesis: A change in the kernel selector scoring (PR #7482) biased towards batched kernels when quantized variants were introduced. Combined with the adaptive batching window being too permissive for short sequences, this increased first-token serialization and delayed start-of-generation across the multiplexed queue. Additionally, KV-cache prewarm was deferred for short sessions which added cold-start overhead.

Mitigation performed so far (short-term):
1) Emergency routing policy: pinned affected customers to the previous kernel-selection profile (rollback flag) to immediately restore prior latency SLOs. (rolled out 2026-03-06 02:15 UTC)
2) Rate-limits/priority-smoothing: applied short-session priority lane and reduced batching window for sessions < 120 tokens in Hosted and Dedicated (hotpatch runtime-config).
3) Manual KV prewarm: lightweight prewarm enabled for pinned sessions to avoid cold KV fetch.
4) Customer comms: notified three escalated customers (Customer Alpha, Beta, Gamma) with interim mitigations and ETA for full fix.

Planned permanent fix:
- Introduce per-variant batching windows and a short-session fast-path that bypasses aggressive kernel-batching for sequences under threshold.
- Rework kernel selector score to include session-length penalty and multiplier for quantized models when multi-variant fanout detected.
- Add KV prewarm gating for short sessions with backpressure-safe heuristics.
- Add regression unit + e2e load tests simulating multi-variant fanout with mixed sequence lengths.

Acceptance criteria (see list): defined rollout plan and measurable telemetry improvements.

Notes: This ticket coordinates across runtime, scheduler, and model-onboarding teams. Private deployments require an air-gapped hotfix package; coordinate with Solutions for delivery and rollout windows.
acceptance_criteria: TTFT 95th percentile reduced to <= baseline + 10% for short-session traffic on canary after rollout
tokens/sec for short sessions restored to within 90% of pre-regression baseline in perf benchmarks
per-variant batching window implemented and configurable via runtime config with sane defaults
end-to-end tests covering mixed-variant fanout and short/long session mixes added to CI
customer Alpha/Beta/Gamma confirm restored latencies in Dedicated and Private environments
